correctness.rationale: Set S=ΣRᵢ²/σ² and Wᵢ=Rᵢ²/(σ²S). The chi-square total is independent of the Dirichlet proportions, and selection depends only on the latter. For m>1, E[W_I^(−p/2)] is comparable to E[W₁^((α−p)/2)] since ΣWᵢ^(α/2) is uniformly bounded above and below by positive constants. The beta density gives p<d+α; S contributes p<md. Both endpoints are excluded, and m=1 reduces directly to the chi law. The selected direction is uniform and the selected measurement independent with finite nonzero moments of every positive order. Orthogonality gives the innovation as a norm lower bound, with the triangle inequality giving finite-time finiteness below threshold. For d≥2, E||Qv||^p=q_p||v||^p with q_p<1 provides a summable backward series in L¹ and finite p-moment by Minkowski or subadditivity. Synchronous contraction conditional on arbitrary finite initial displacements proves uniqueness without assuming second moments; for d=1 the update is a fresh draw. Orthogonality transfers divergence to stationarity. At α=2 the selected proportion is its size-biased beta; multiplying its negative moment by the independent chi-square negative moment gives the stated gamma formula (the m=1 simplification is consistent). At p=2 the innovation contributes mτ²/[σ²(md−2)] and the contraction is 1−1/d, giving the stated risk including the divergent cases.
residual_risks: All claims rely on fresh independent sampling; neither a repeated fixed random design nor reuse of the offset is justified by this argument. The deterministic-seed Monte Carlo is illustrative, not decisive at the divergence boundary.
